summary:
I've been building a personal assistant to replace the agent I'd been running at home. It's a Telegram bot with a small browser app on top. Models run on my own hardware for anything private, and Claude handles the rest. The line between the two is enforced by separate unix users on each machine, not by a prompt asking nicely. Private answers can come back, but the raw messages and mail stay with the local model. The first version took a night. The second night went to a client API, a phone UI with voice, and a pairing flow. A 48-character token is hard to type on a phone, so the app takes a six-digit code instead.

Most of the hard bugs were small and specific. A Python SDK quietly loaded every tool server configured for my own account, so each turn carried roughly 190K tokens of context I never asked for. Strict mode fixed that. One tool server alone cost about 65K tokens per session, so I deferred it and kept the rest near 21K. On the phone, iOS Safari wouldn't play Opus audio, so the app serves MP3 and Telegram keeps Opus for voice notes. Home-screen apps also came up 62 pixels short of the screen, and the fix was a single CSS rule for standalone mode.

On TheWordGroup, I've been rebuilding it on Fastify, TypeScript and Postgres.

I also spent time on a D&D campaign tool, mostly access rules. A character sheet can now carry a hidden relationship, like a lieutenant secretly serving a villain, and players only see a link when both ends are visible to them. The database enforces the rule, not just the UI. I also fixed a Select component that showed raw IDs instead of labels, then added a lint rule so a new one can't ship the same way.

On the infrastructure side, I wrote a small deadman check for Syncthing after a full disk left it dead for nine days without anyone noticing. It now runs every fifteen minutes, and the morning briefing reports on it daily.

highlights.oneLiner: Retired its Claude auth, moved every model role onto the local brain.
Routes private model work to the local GPU, keeping raw messages off Claude.
Rebuilding on Fastify, TypeScript and Postgres, phases 0 to 3 done.
Added a Syncthing deadman check after a full disk left sync dead nine days.
